topic.name: Approximating Values Using the Binomial Theorem

question.text: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(1.02)^{7}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^7$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to two decimal places.
question.explanation:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer,

\[ (1+x)^n = 1 + nx + \dfrac{1}{2!} n(n-1)x^2 + \cdots + x^n. \]

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \left( {1 + x} \right)^7 &= 1 + 7x + \dfrac{1}{2!} \cdot 7 \cdot 6\cdot x^2 + \cdots + x^n\\[5pt] &= 1 + 7x + 21x^2 + \cdots + x^n. \end{align*}

So, for small $x,$ we have \[ {\left( {1 + x} \right)^{7}} \approx 1 + 7x + 21x^2. \]

Now, we substitute $x = 0.02$ into the above approximation of $(1 + x)^7{:}$ \begin{align*} (1.02)^7 & = (1 + 0.02)^7 \\[5pt] & \approx 1 + 7(0.02) + 21(0.02)^2 \\[5pt] & = 1 + 7(0.02) + 21(0.000\,4) \\[5pt] & = 1 + 0.14 + 0.008\,4 \\[5pt] & = 1.148\,4 \end{align*}

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: \begin{align*} \% \: \rm{ error}&= \dfrac{\textrm{amount of error}}{\textrm{exact value}} \times 100 \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{|(1.02)^7 - 1.148\,4|}{(1.02)^7} \times 100\\[5pt] & \approx 0.02\% \end{align*} rounded to two decimal places.

question.text: Use the first four terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^6$ in ascending powers of $x$ to approximate $(0.84)^6.$ Give your answer to five decimal places.
question.explanation:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer,

\[ (1+x)^n = 1 + nx + \dfrac{1}{2!} n(n-1)x^2 + \dfrac{1}{3!} n(n-1)(n-2)x^3 + \cdots + x^n. \]

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \left( {1 + x} \right)^6 &= 1 +6x + \dfrac12\cdot 6\cdot 5 \cdot x^2 + \dfrac16\cdot 6\cdot 5 \cdot 4 \cdot x^3 + \cdots + x^6 \\[5pt] &= 1 + 6x + 15x^2 +20x^3 + \cdots \, +x^6. \end{align*}

So, for small $x,$ we have

\[ \left( {1 + x} \right)^6 \approx 1 + 6x + 15x^2 + 20x^3. \]

Finally, we substitute $x=-0.16$ into the above approximation of $(1 + x)^6{:}$

\begin{align*} (0.84)^6 &= (1+(-0.16))^6 \\[5pt] &\approx 1 + 6(-0.16) + 15(-0.16)^2 + 20(-0.16)^3 \\[5pt] & = 1 - 6(0.16) + 15(0.025\,6) - 20(0.004\,096)\\[5pt] & = 1 - 0.96 + 0.384 - 0.081\,92\\[5pt] & = 0.342\,08, \end{align*}

to five decimal places.

question.text: Use the first four terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^9$ in ascending powers of $x$ to approximate $(0.92)^9.$ Round your answer to three decimal places.
question.explanation:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, \[ (1+x)^n = 1 + nx + \dfrac{1}{2!} n(n-1)x^2 + \dfrac{1}{3!} n(n-1)(n-2)x^3 + \cdots + x^n. \]

Therefore, \begin{align*} \left( {1 + x} \right)^9 &= 1 +9x + \dfrac12\cdot 9\cdot 8 \cdot x^2 + \dfrac16\cdot 9\cdot 8 \cdot 7 \cdot x^3 + \cdots + x^9 \\[5pt] &= 1 + 9x + 36x^2 +84x^3 + \cdots \, +x^9. \end{align*}

So, for small $x,$ we have \[ \left( {1 + x} \right)^9 \approx 1 + 9x + 36x^2 + 84x^3. \]

Finally, we substitute $x=-0.08$ into the above approximation of $(1 + x)^9{:}$ \begin{align*} (0.92)^9 &= (1+(-0.08))^9 \\[5pt] &\approx 1 + 9(-0.08) + 36(-0.08)^2 + 84(-0.08)^3 \\[5pt] & = 1 - 9(0.08) + 36(0.006\,4) - 84(0.000\,512)\\[5pt] & = 1 - 0.72 + 0.2304 - 0.043\,008 \\[5pt] & \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ 0.467} \end{align*} rounded to three decimal places.
